instruction: Rank the four statements from 1 to 4: 1 for the one most like you, 4 for the one least like you. Every number is used once. There are no better or worse answers — the point is what you put first when you cannot put everything first.

processing.name: Processing
processing.negativeDescription: by watching and going over it

active.name: Active
active.short: learning from being in the experience itself
active.description: Learns from being in the experience. Bored by preamble, takes energy from novelty and from other people, and will have joined in before the instructions are finished. The point of the cycle where something actually happens.

reflective.name: Reflective
reflective.short: learning by stepping back and going over what happened
reflective.description: Watches before acting. Gathers what happened, thinks before speaking, and wants time and some distance before committing to a view. Often the person who noticed the thing nobody else did.

theorist.name: Theorist
theorist.short: learning by building an explanation that holds together
theorist.description: Wants the model and the reasoning. Uncomfortable with an activity whose purpose has not been stated, and works by fitting new things into a system that already holds together.

pragmatist.name: Pragmatist
pragmatist.short: learning by trying ideas out to see what works
pragmatist.description: Wants to try the idea out. Tests it against practice, asks what it looks like with a real group, plans the next step, and loses patience with theory that does not arrive anywhere.

sets.prompt: A session opens with an activity I have never done before.

statements.active: I join in straight away and work out what is going on while doing it.
statements.reflective: I wait and watch how the first people handle it.
statements.theorist: I want to be told what the activity is for before it starts.
statements.pragmatist: I want to know what I will be able to do with it afterwards.

sets.prompt: The group is discussing an idea and I have something to say.

statements.active: I start talking before the thought is finished and shape it as I go.
statements.reflective: I wait until I have worked out what I think, even if the moment passes.
statements.theorist: I try to connect what people are saying into one explanation before adding to it.
statements.pragmatist: I ask for an example of the idea being used with a real group.

sets.prompt: I am sent something to read before a session.

statements.active: I read it quickly and rely on the session itself.
statements.reflective: I read all of it and write notes, even when there is more than I need.
statements.theorist: I look for the reasoning behind what the text claims.
statements.pragmatist: I look for the parts I can use and leave the rest.

sets.prompt: A session I took part in has just ended.

statements.active: I am already thinking about the next thing to do.
statements.reflective: I go back over what happened before I decide what I think of it.
statements.theorist: I try to fit what happened into what I already thought about the subject.
statements.pragmatist: I choose one thing to do differently the next time I run a session.

sets.prompt: The plan has to change with very little warning.

statements.active: I improvise and find out what works while it is happening.
statements.reflective: I want a few minutes to think before I say anything.
statements.theorist: I want to understand why the change is needed before I agree to it.
statements.pragmatist: I look for the option that works with the people and the time we have now.

sets.prompt: Someone shows me a method I might use in my own sessions.

statements.active: I would rather try it and adjust it than plan it out first.
statements.reflective: I would rather watch someone else use it a few times first.
statements.theorist: I would rather understand the thinking it comes from first.
statements.pragmatist: I would rather be given the steps so that I can use it at once.
